# Phase 2 Single-Arm Study of Pembrolizumab in Advanced Melanoma: BRAF Mutation Status Does Not Predict Response

## Background

Pembrolizumab, an anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody, has demonstrated durable responses in advanced melanoma. BRAF mutation status has been proposed as a predictive biomarker, but its relationship to anti-PD-1 efficacy remains incompletely characterized. This Phase 2, single-arm study (NCT03882047) evaluated pembrolizumab monotherapy in unresectable or metastatic melanoma and assessed outcomes by BRAF mutation status.

## Methods

Patients with histologically confirmed unresectable Stage III or Stage IV melanoma, ECOG performance status 0-1, and no prior systemic therapy for advanced disease were enrolled. All patients received pembrolizumab 200 mg intravenously every 3 weeks (Q3W) until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, or completion of 35 cycles (approximately 2 years). BRAF V600 mutation testing was performed centrally using a validated PCR assay. Prespecified subgroup analyses by BRAF mutation status (BRAF-mutant vs. BRAF wild-type), PD-L1 expression (TPS ≥1% vs. <1%), and LDH level (elevated vs. normal) were conducted, but these subgroups were not separate randomized arms.

## Results

One hundred twelve patients were enrolled (BRAF-mutant: n=47, 42%; BRAF wild-type: n=65, 58%). All 112 patients received pembrolizumab 200 mg Q3W on the single treatment arm. The confirmed overall response rate (ORR) was 38% (95% CI 29–48). Median progression-free survival (mPFS) was 6.8 months (95% CI 4.3–10.1). In the BRAF-mutant subgroup, ORR was 40% vs. 37% in the BRAF wild-type subgroup (p=0.74), consistent with the primary analysis. Subgroup analyses for PD-L1 TPS ≥1% showed ORR of 45% versus 26% in TPS <1% patients; however, these represent post-hoc analyses of the same single pembrolizumab arm and should not be interpreted as separate treatment groups. Grade 3-4 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 18% of patients.

## Conclusion

Pembrolizumab monotherapy demonstrated meaningful clinical activity in advanced melanoma irrespective of BRAF mutation status. BRAF mutation, PD-L1 expression, and LDH stratifications are subgroup analyses within a single-arm trial and do not represent separate treatment arms. These findings support pembrolizumab as a first-line treatment option regardless of BRAF mutational status.
